findings.summary: The new recipe accepts nonempty owner hierarchy authorization but unattended startup has no protected source for it.
findings.evidence: tpm-contracts.md:31–36,63–66,197–205; design.md:28–38. The local seal/recover pipe carries owner_auth, while serve exposes only bundle/profile and intentionally persists no hierarchy secret. Recreating the owner primary requires that hierarchy authorization.
findings.fix: Simplest first profile: support only empty owner hierarchy auth, reject nonempty enrollment/recovery input and qualified profiles before publication, and add refusal/boot fixtures. Alternatively define an actual unattended protected boot input that meets the no-external-call/no-clear-disk rules. Do not seal a candidate that cannot boot.

findings.summary: Required isolated local swtpm coverage has no route through the new fixed production device, owner-state and protected-host contracts.
findings.evidence: design.md:28–29,121–124; tpm-contracts.md:76–103,125–172. Production owner always opens /dev/tpmrm0 and fixed root-owned /run state, but make tpm-test promises private swtpm sockets and no physical TPM access. No isolated transport/record/profile injection or sandbox setup is specified.
findings.fix: Define an explicit test-only integration route (for example a test-binary transport/host-facts/state-path constructor plus isolated private swtpm socket and real protected-memory fixtures) without a shipping runtime bypass. Specify how CI sets required permissions/limits and exercises the production owner protocol while proving it never opens the host TPM/state. Required cases must run, not silently skip.

findings.summary: Common preflight scope says any secret read, but failed preflight still starts ordinary TLS/token-authenticated metadata RPCs.
findings.evidence: design.md:34–39; tpm-contracts.md:148–152. Existing identity/token secrets are explicitly outside #57 intent scope.
findings.fix: Name the covered TPM source material (KEK, canary, escrow/unlock and hierarchy-auth inputs) and state that baseline TLS/token loading remains governed by existing setup. Apply the wording consistently.
